newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea's Kim praises Deng as "comrade-in-arms".
newsitem.headline: N.Korea's Kim praises Deng as "comrade-in-arms".

text.p: Communist North Korea's de facto leader Kim Jong-il on Thursday praised China's Deng Xiaoping as an "intimate friend and comrade-in-arms" of the Korean people and said his death was a great loss to them.

"I, in the name of...the entire Korean people and in my own, extend deep condolences to you and...to the government of the People's Republic of China, the fraternal Chinese people and the bereaved family," the Korea Central News Agency (KCNA) quoted Kim as saying in a message to Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
Kim praised Deng's historic contribution to China's communist party and to the Chinese revolution, KCNA said in a report monitored in Tokyo.
"His death is a great loss, not only to the Chinese party and people but also to the Korean people," Kim said. "He was an intimate friend and comrade-in-arms of the Korean people."
Kim said Deng had "forged a particular intimacy" with Kim Il-sung, his father and North Korea's leader until his death in 1994.
"The exploits performed by him for the Korea-China friendship will remain forever in the hearts of the Korean people," Kim said.
China's official news agency reported that Deng, China's paramount leader, died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection, aged 92.
On Thursday, analysts in Tokyo described Deng's death as a blow to North Korea's old-style communist leaders, for whom China has been a key ally.

The two countries fought side by side against the United States and South Korea in the 1950-53 Korean War, but in recent years China has established diplomatic relations and business ties with Pyongyang's arch-rival, capitalist South Korea.
